children: The search_synonyms table — manual and machine-learned query rewrites that are expanded before either search engine runs.
search_synonyms holds query-expansion rows that Search applies before ranking. Each row has a
— curated by an operator (domain aliases, brand spellings).
— minted by the Auto Correction Loop as an alt_correction once a Did You Mean suggestion is accepted across ≥2 distinct sessions in Search Intelligence.
The alt_correction column carries the corrected form a typo should expand into — headless for hadless.
Synonyms are not an engine feature; they are a pre-engine transform. QueryPipeline's expand_synonyms step rewrites the incoming query

, which is precisely why a single synonym row reaches both Postgres Search and the Indx Engine without either engine knowing it happened. Postgres then matches the expanded terms against its Search Vector; Indx feeds them into BM25F.

Putting expansion upstream keeps the two engines behind one honest Search contract: corrections, aliases, and learned fixes are applied in exactly one place, so the engines never drift in how they interpret a query. The downstream effect of synonym expansion on relevance is one of the levers the Golden Eval harness measures.
